scope: Blind Guides01, Mote/Beam01 and Tree/Fruit01–02 original-detail review for dignity, anatomy, symbolic object comparison, fig plausibility and source boundaries.
globalConditions: Technical review is not owner approval or final browser acceptance.
Illustrative comparisons must not become unsupported historical, medical or botanical claims.

entries.recommendedTitle: The need for a trustworthy guide
entries.alt: Two travelers move beside a rough ditch; the older man holds a wooden staff while the younger man behind him rests a hand on his upper arm.
entries.caption: Jesus asks whether a blind person can lead another blind person without both falling into a ditch. The travelers illustrate His comparison about guidance, without equating physical disability with moral failure.
entries.findings: Distinct younger dark-haired and older gray-haired travelers rendered with dignity; no fall or injury. Staff grip, upper-arm contact, walking legs and sandals credible. Eyes appear downcast but cannot establish visual diagnosis; alt properly describes observable action. Photographic skin, garments and terrain.
conditions: Do not diagnose blindness from pixels or characterize blindness as personal moral inferiority.
No completed fall, rescue or injury is shown; literal travelers are an illustration of Jesus' question.

entries.alt: A large rough wooden beam rests on a workshop bench beside a tiny wood splinter displayed on dark cloth.
entries.caption: Jesus contrasts noticing a mote in another person's eye with overlooking a beam in one's own. The large timber and tiny splinter picture His call to examine ourselves before correcting someone else.
entries.findings: Clear proportional comparison of huge timber and small splinter. Natural wood grain, cracks, shavings and bench support. No human eye, injury, embedded labels or literal impossible beam penetration; symbolic still life successfully avoids bodily harm depiction.
conditions: Workshop arrangement illustrates the verbal comparison; not an event Jesus is recorded arranging.
Objects' sizes are illustrative, not exact source measurements.

entries.alt: Green and purple figs hang from a branch among broad lobed leaves, with a sunlit hillside beyond.
entries.caption: Jesus teaches that a good tree does not bring forth corrupt fruit, nor a corrupt tree good fruit. The fig-bearing branch pictures the connection between a tree and what it produces.
entries.findings: Recognizable fig form with broad lobed palmate-veined foliage and green/purple pear-shaped fruit attached to woody branch. No visible rot or impossible mixed species. Photographic fruit skin, leaf veins and bark, plausible overall botanical illustration.
conditions: Image does not establish taste, ripeness of every fig, exact cultivar or authenticated historical tree.
The fruit comparison is teaching imagery, not a diagnosis of people's worth from appearance.

entries.recommendedTitle: Figs are not gathered from thorns
entries.alt: A thorn-covered shrub with sparse small leaves grows among rocks on a dry hillside; no figs or grapes are visible.
entries.caption: Jesus says that each tree is known by its fruit: figs are not gathered from thorns, nor grapes from a bramble. The thorny branches illustrate the contrast with the fruit-bearing tree.
entries.findings: Coherent branching thorn shrub, sparse leaves and natural dry landscape. No visible figs or grapes; no mislabeled fruit object. Photographic bark and thorns; species kept generic rather than unsupported identification.
conditions: Absence of figs or grapes is the relevant visible distinction; do not claim every thorny species is incapable of producing any fruit.
Specific shrub species and location are not authenticated or required by the source.
